text: Owner framing (2026-10-13): this is a small throwaway weekend fun project. Owner accepts the risk of Pi Durable (experimental, breaking changes weekly) and chose Durable plus pi-env over the coding-agent SDK plus hand-written SSH tools. Reason: Durable already does background subagents, a stored inbox with requestId dedupe, crash resume, and cost totals; the SDK path would mean writing those ourselves. Pin pi-durable and pi-env to 1.2.0. Keep scope minimal; do not build for longevity.

Owner instruction (2026-10-13): although the README is cheeky and this is partly an art project, the agents themselves must take the goal (make money ethically) seriously. No jokes or character play in founder or worker prompts. Also: the harness SSH key for local development lives at .secrets/ssh/id_ed25519 (gitignored); in deployment it is /data/ssh/id_ed25519 in the Harbormaster data volume.

Advisors use the owner's Claude and ChatGPT subscriptions through pi-ai OAuth login (credential file copied to /data/auth.json, file-backed CredentialStore so refreshes persist). Checked 2026-10-13: Anthropic bills third-party-tool OAuth use as 'extra usage' at API rates since 2026-04-04 and no longer blocks it; the official 'claude -p' would draw from plan limits instead. Owner accepted the extra-usage cost for simplicity. Rejected: official CLIs as subprocesses (two binaries, two credential formats). Also rejected: API keys (owner wants the subscriptions used).

Operational facts from the 2026-10-13 build session. (1) Developer test runs drove the real founder against the real VM; it built an uptime product 'Beacon' under /srv/company with systemd units and a /company/company.db. The VM and the local .secrets/data/harness.sqlite are therefore not clean; wipe both before the first real deployment unless the owner wants to keep that start. (2) The installed Harbormaster is 0.3.4, which only finds docker-compose.yml, so the compose file is named that, not compose.yml. (3) The founder answered the owner's first 'Hi' only after ~10 bash calls inspecting the VM; a slow first reply is normal, not a bug. (4) Rejected in final review: serializing the stop-flag check with submissions; a heartbeat or owner message can slip in right after a cost-cap stop, costing one extra turn before the next 60 s cap check stops it again. Accepted for simplicity.

2026-10-13 owner report: the founder was silent on Telegram because owner messages queued as follow-ups behind long founder runs (it was running, about $1 per 10 minutes on deepseek-v4.1-flash, so the $20 daily cap trips in roughly 3 hours of continuous work). Fix: owner messages steer (whenBusy 'steer'), a background wait reports an 'unanswered' settlement to the owner, and the founder prompt requires a message_owner reply first. Rejected: forwarding the founder's plain assistant text to Telegram automatically. It needs an event watcher and would also forward replies to heartbeats, which the owner does not want. Note: Durable does not pass a failed founder run to onReport; only the submission settlement shows it.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: 2026-10-13 owner decision: the heartbeat interval goes from 30 minutes to 6 hours because the founder ran continuously and hit the daily cost cap in about 3 hours. In its place the founder got one-shot wake-up tools (schedule_wakeup, list_wakeups, cancel_wakeup) so it can end a turn and come back at a time it chooses. The owner chose one-shot only and no cap on delay. Rejected: recurring (cron-like) schedules, because a forgotten recurring timer burns money with no owner action; a one-shot that re-schedules itself gives the same effect. Rejected: a real cron on the VM, because the VM never connects to the harness, so it has nothing to call. The live interval is in /data/config.json on the server, which the owner edits by hand; the repo only changes config.example.json.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: Web search and fetch use Ollama's web API (https://ollama.com/api/web_search, /api/web_fetch) with the existing OLLAMA_API_KEY. DeepSeek's Search/Fetch API (api.deepseek.com/v1/tools/search, /fetch; $0.75 per 1000 successful calls, 5 QPS) was considered and not used: it needs a separate DeepSeek platform account, prepaid balance, and key, while the company only has an Ollama Cloud key. Ollama's billing for web search was not confirmed as of 2026-10-18: a Sept 2025 blog post says it is free with rate limits, the current credit-based pricing page does not mention it. The owner chose not to check before shipping. If Ollama's limits or costs turn out bad, swap the backend in src/web.ts to DeepSeek; the tool interface does not need to change. Neither backend counts toward the daily cost cap.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: 2026-10-18 owner approved send_file as founder-only, documents only. Rejected: worker access or a per-role switch (spec says workers do not message the owner; they report file paths and the founder sends), sendPhoto for images (compresses the file, second code path), and inbound files from the owner (bot still ignores non-text messages; a separate ticket if wanted).
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>
